claims.text: Pre-processing reweighting produces negligible fairness improvement across regions when structural disparities are embedded within the feature space.
Baseline logistic regression exhibits persistent threshold collapse across regions, with false positive rates exceeding 0.913 and reaching 1.0 in four regions.

Post-processing isotonic calibration improves AUC-ROC in North America to approximately 0.780 but degrades AUC-ROC in South Asia to approximately 0.594, Sub-Saharan Africa to 0.667, and Latin America to 0.656.
Demographic parity disparities in Sub-Saharan Africa remain resistant to post-hoc mitigation strategies, retaining the highest disparity gap across evaluated models.

Performance costs of fairness interventions are geographically asymmetric, reducing F1 score by 0.014 in Sub-Saharan Africa for only a 0.007 reduction in Demographic Parity Gap, while high-resource regions remain unaffected.
In South Asia, post-processing isotonic calibration degrades both performance and fairness, decreasing F1 from 0.911 to 0.909 and worsening Demographic Parity Gap from 0.103 to 0.110.

evidence.description: Pre-processing reweighting produced no measurable fairness improvement across regions, with absolute differences below 0.001 across aggregate metrics and below 0.002 across regional AUC-ROC relative to baseline.

False Positive Rates exceeded 0.913 across all regions under Baseline LR, with South Asia, East Asia, Western Europe, and North America recording FPR = 1.000, revealing that high aggregate recall (0.999) was an artefact of threshold collapse.

Calibrated GBM produced an AUC-ROC of ≈0.780 in North America but dropped to ≈0.594 in South Asia, ≈0.667 in Sub-Saharan Africa, and ≈0.656 in Latin America, with statistically significant reductions confirmed via bootstrap confidence intervals.
Sub-Saharan Africa recorded DPG = 0.018 in Baseline LR, remained at 0.018 under Reweighted LR, and remained consistently the highest disparity across all models.

Sub-Saharan Africa experienced an F1 reduction from 0.876 to 0.862 (net Δ = -0.014) for a DPG reduction from 0.180 to 0.173 (gain of 0.007) under calibrated GBM, whereas Western Europe (0.970) and North America (0.980) maintained flat F1 scores.
For South Asia, calibrated GBM decreased F1 from 0.911 to 0.909 (Δ = -0.002) while DPG worsened from 0.103 to 0.110.

methodologies.name: Cross-Regional Bias Detection and Mitigation Pipeline
methodologies.description: A five-stage evaluation pipeline assessing pre-processing reweighting and post-processing isotonic calibration against a baseline logistic regression across four fairness metrics in six world regions.
datasets: Synthetic cross-regional dataset parameterised from World Bank Development Indicators (2023), ILO Labour Statistics (2023), and Global Findex (2022)
conditions: Fairness-Aware Reweighted Logistic Regression with inverse regional frequency weights
Gradient Boosting Classifier with 5-fold stratified cross-validation and post-hoc isotonic regression calibration
Train-test stratified split (75% train, 25% test, N=6,000 total)

limitations.text: The synthetic dataset, while parameterised from empirical distributional statistics, cannot fully replicate the intersectional complexity and institutional variability of real administrative records.
Only three debiasing strategies were evaluated, leaving other fairness-aware approaches like adversarial debiasing, fair representation learning, and constrained optimisation unexamined.
The study evaluated binary classification outcomes exclusively and does not extend to multi-class classification, ranking systems, or regression settings.
The analysis focused primarily on geographic disparity and did not incorporate intersectional subgroup analysis involving gender, ethnicity, disability, or language.
Access to large-scale, ethically shareable, cross-regional administrative datasets remains highly restricted due to privacy, governance, and institutional barriers.
Most existing fairness studies evaluate fairness interventions on only one or two protected attributes within a single national context, typically the United States.

future_work.text: Validate findings using real-world administrative datasets.
Extend the bias mitigation and evaluation framework to intersectional and multi-class prediction settings.
Evaluate additional debiasing methods, including adversarial debiasing, fair representation learning, and constrained Pareto-optimal optimisation, within the pipeline architecture.
